topic: What if you brought a modern car to ancient Rome?

script.text: Here's where you are. Rome, the year one thirteen. The emperor Trajan rules everything from the Atlantic to the Red Sea. And Rome is the biggest city on Earth, with maybe a million people. That's real.
Here's what you've got. One ordinary car. A full tank, enough for about six hundred kilometers. Two phones with no signal. A charger. Half a bag of chips. And Mo's playlist.
The car works perfectly. The engine, the lights, the horn, the speakers. Nothing in this world can stop it.
But here's the rule. The nearest gas station is about eighteen hundred years away. Every drop of fuel you burn is gone forever.
And one more thing. As far as you know, yours is the only engine on the planet. The only one. Remember that.

science.claim: Rome around AD 100 was the largest city on Earth, with perhaps about a million people.
science.working: Modern estimates for Rome's population in the early 2nd century AD range from about 450,000 to over 1 million; it was the largest city of its time.
science.source: Wikipedia: Population of ancient Rome; G. Storey, 'The population of ancient Rome', Antiquity 71 (1997)
